items.title: Smetti di pagare il cloud ogni mese: ecco i NAS UGREEN scontati per la Festa delle Offerte Prime
items.summary: Lo sai quanto spenderai in abbonamenti cloud negli anni in cui custodirai i tuoi documenti e le tue foto? Con un NAS paghi una volta sola, e dal 6 all'11 ottobre UGREEN ha in sconto sei dispositivi ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Dal 6 ottobre Amazon apre la Festa delle Offerte Prime, 48 ore di sconti riservati agli abbonati Prime, e UGREEN concentra in questi due giorni i ribassi più alti della sua promozione d'autunno sui NAS NASync : sei modelli scontati sia su Amazon sia sul sito del produttore.

Un NAS (Network Attached Storage) collega al router uno o più hard disk e li rende raggiungibili da telefoni, computer e televisori, sia sulla rete di casa sia da fuori tramite Internet.

Il secondo argomento riguarda il controllo dei dati, poiché foto, documenti e backup restano sui dischi di casa e non passano dai server di terzi.

Per tutti i NASync è presente la cifratura delle connessioni con TLS/SSL, RSA e AES , l'autenticazione a due fattori e un Security Manager che controlla il sistema in modo continuo. I NAS hanno ottenuto anche la certificazione di sicurezza ETSI EN 303 645, rilasciata da TÜV SÜD, e quella statunitense TRUSTe. Anche il riconoscimento dei volti e degli oggetti nell'app Foto gira sul NAS senza inviare le immagini a servizi esterni.

C'è poi la velocità. Dentro casa i trasferimenti dipendono dalla rete locale e non dalla linea internet in upload, che nelle connessioni domestiche resta di solito il collo di bottiglia, specialmente se non si ha una fibra seria. Su una porta a 2,5 Gb/s si arriva a un massimo teorico di 312,5 MB/s, che vuol dire copiare un video 4K da 20 GB in poco più di un minuto.

È facile anche la configurazione, che sui NAS UGREEN richiede meno di dieci minuti e un'unica app per gestire file, backup delle foto e streaming verso la TV.

La prima decisione riguarda il numero di alloggiamenti per i dischi . Con due dischi si può impostare il RAID 1, che scrive gli stessi dati su entrambi: se un disco si guasta, i file restano sull'altro, ma la capienza utile è alla fine quella di un solo disco perché il secondo serve come sicurezza. Con quattro o sei alloggiamenti si possono usare il RAID 5 e il RAID 6, che salvano su tutti i dischi anche delle informazioni di controllo; quindi se un disco si rompe (due, con il RAID 6), il NAS ricostruisce i file mancanti a partire da quelli rimasti.

Conviene pensare a quanto crescerà l'archivio nei prossimi anni, perché quando tutti gli alloggiamenti saranno occupati, per avere più spazio bisognerà sostituire i dischi con altri più capienti, uno alla volta, oppure collegare un'unità esterna. Partire con un NAS a quattro alloggiamenti e due soli dischi lascia invece margine per aggiungerne altri due in seguito.

La seconda riguarda il processore. I modelli della serie DH di UGREEN usano chip ARM di Rockchip, poco energivori e sufficienti per archivio, backup e streaming , con una versione semplificata del sistema operativo UGOS Pro e memoria non espandibile.

La serie DXP monta processori Intel, ha la versione completa di UGOS Pro, memoria espandibile e due slot M.2 per SSD da usare come cache o come spazio aggiuntivo. È quindi la strada per chi vuole affiancare all'archivio carichi più pesanti , come le macchine virtuali o un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, oppure servire molti utenti insieme.

La terza e ultima scelta è quella della rete . Una porta da 1 Gb/s basta per foto e documenti, quella da 2,5 Gb/s è utile con i video pesanti, mentre i 10 Gb/s servono a chi lavora in rete su file di grandi dimensioni e ha computer e switch in grado di sfruttarli.

Il DH2300 è pensato per chi un NAS non l'ha mai avuto e vuole soprattutto mettere al sicuro le foto di famiglia, smettendo di rincorrere lo spazio libero sul telefono. Ha due alloggiamenti: con due dischi in RAID 1 ogni file viene salvato due volte e, se uno dei dischi si guasta, l'archivio resta intatto. Si configura dall'app UGREEN con una procedura guidata e, per collegare lo smartphone, basta avvicinarlo al NAS grazie all'NFC .

Collegato al televisore del salotto tramite l'uscita HDMI 4K, riproduce film e video di casa senza bisogno di un computer . Il processore Rockchip a otto core e i 4 GB di memoria bastano per archivio, backup e streaming, con una capienza che arriva a 64 TB complessivi.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DH2300, da listino di 246,99 euro, scende a 189,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Quando i dispositivi da salvare diventano tanti, tra gli smartphone di tutta la famiglia, i portatili e magari il lavoro da casa, due dischi si riempiono in fretta. Il DH4300 Plus raddoppia gli alloggiamenti, fino a 128 TB, e permette di scegliere il RAID 5 o il RAID 6 , che proteggono i dati sacrificando meno spazio.

La porta di rete a 2,5 Gb/s accorcia i tempi quando si salvano video pesanti, e il processore Rockchip RK3588C con 8 GB di memoria regge più persone collegate insieme. Chi ha un po' di dimestichezza può installare applicazioni aggiuntive tramite Docker , mentre per tutti gli altri restano la configurazione guidata e l'app unica del DH2300.

Nei giorni della Festa delle Offerte Prime, e fino all'11 ottobre, il prezzo scende da 439,99 euro a 319,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP4800 Plus è il modello per chi dal NAS vuole qualcosa in più di un archivio , quindi un server multimediale che converte i video al volo, qualche macchina virtuale, i backup automatici di tutti i computer di casa o dello studio.

Il processore Intel Pentium Gold a cinque core lavora con 8 GB di memoria DDR5, espandibili fino a 64 GB, e il sistema gira su un SSD dedicato da 128 GB.

Accanto ai quattro alloggiamenti per hard disk ci sono due slot per SSD M.2 , da usare come cache per velocizzare i file aperti più spesso con una capienza massima di 144 TB.

La porta da 10 Gb/s, affiancata da una seconda a 2,5 Gb/s, serve a chi lavora su file grandi da un computer collegato via cavo, e il lettore di schede SD permette di scaricare le foto della fotocamera direttamente sul NAS.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il prezzo scende da 729,99 euro a 549,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con sei alloggiamenti per hard disk e due per SSD, il DXP6800 Pro si rivolge a un piccolo studio professionale o a chi custodisce un archivio video di anni perché può arrivare fino a 208 TB di spazio.

Il processore Intel Core i5 a dieci core permette a più persone di lavorare contemporaneamente sugli stessi file, anche mentre il NAS esegue i backup o converte un video.

Le due porte di rete da 10 Gb/s si possono unire fino a 20 Gb/s , e le due Thunderbolt 4 servono a collegare dischi esterni veloci, per esempio per scaricare il materiale di una giornata di riprese. L 'uscita HDMI arriva fino all'8K.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre il DXP6800 Pro è in offerta, passando dal listino di 1.209,99 euro a 899,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP2800 è per chi si accontenta di due dischi ma dal NAS vuole più di un archivio di foto. Ha gli stessi due alloggiamenti del DH2300, ma monta un processore Intel più potente e la versione completa del sistema UGOS Pro , con più applicazioni a disposizione. La memoria si può ampliare fino a 16 GB e due slot per SSD servono a velocizzare i file usati più spesso.

Dal 6 all'11 ottobre si scende dal listino di 439,99 euro a 329,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Il DXP480T Plus rinuncia agli hard disk e accoglie quattro SSD M.2 NVMe , così da lavorare sui file video direttamente dalla rete senza rallentamenti. Monta lo stesso Core i5 del DXP6800 Pro, una porta da 10 Gb/s e due Thunderbolt 4.

In questo caso lo sconto vale solo il 6 e 7 ottobre: in quei due giorni il prezzo di listino di 999,99 euro passa a 749,99 euro su Amazon e sul sito ufficiale di UGREEN .

Con la Festa delle Offerte Prime è il momento giusto per smettere di pagare lo spazio online ogni mese e riportare a casa i propri ricordi, una volta per tutte.

Sui NAS UGREEN i prezzi della festa restano validi dal 6 fino all'11 ottobre su tutti i modelli tranne il DXP480T Plus, che sale dal prezzo scontato di 749,99 euro a 899,99 euro già dall'8 ottobre. Tutte le offerte sono sulla pagina UGREEN di Amazon e sulla pagina dedicata del sito UGREEN .

items.title: Why isn't the industry freaking out about DeepSeek 4.1 Flash?
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.dgt.is/blog/2026-10-07-deepseek-freek-out/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50000488 Points: 347 # Comments: 298
items.content:
I have been using DeepSeek 4.1 Flash for about a month, heavily, across a dozen projects. It is super capable, and orders of magnitude cheaper than the "frontier" models. When I'm mid-session, if I don't look at the model name, I honestly could not tell you if I'm using DeepSeek or Opus. Whether it's our conversations, the work, or the speed, I don't notice a difference. I don't care that there is no 4.1 "Pro". I treat this like a frontier model because it behaves like one . I'm coming at this from my subjective usage experience, but you can see more complete benchmarks here if that floats your boat.

So why aren't the frontier labs freaking out right now? China is going to eat their lunch. They may be a month or two behind Anthropic/OpenAI, but these distilled Chinese models can handle the same workloads.

Sure, they stole Claude's training , and Anthropic stole it from other people. I'm not getting into the whole who-owns-whose-data debate, because most developers aren't thinking like that. They're just trying to get the most bang for their buck.

Today's models are now good enough for high-quality unattended tasks. Chasing the latest and greatest is silly. It is fun to see the new Fable capabilities, but the tasks we throw at them are usually ridiculous (maybe even insulting) if you believe in LLM sentience. It's like asking a math PhD to organize the files on your desktop.

With my OpenCode Go sub of $10/month, DeepSeek is basically unlimited. This has completely changed my way of developing. There is no shame now in spinning up mindless tasks, or exploratory UI monkey testing. And sure, go ahead and reorganize your desktop files. That will cost $0.003 instead of $1. I have rarely exceeded $1 in expected costs in a session. I try to keep my sessions tight, but sometimes they run for most of a day.

I even lean on 4.1 Flash for complex planning and research. For occasional critical tasks , I sometimes pull in Opus 5.5 to do a final code review, which will catch a few edge cases. Then I have DeepSeek execute the fixes. Even when I call up Opus or GLM (which seems to be drinking the same Chinese Kool-Aid as DeepSeek), it's less about quality and capabilities and more about getting new eyes on a problem.

DeepSeek shrank the KV cache by roughly 437x compared to their V1 model. Holding that cache in GPU memory is one of the biggest costs of running long coding sessions. That's how my all-day sessions stay under a dollar.

It must be better for the environment too. Using Claude almost feels wasteful, and not just on cost: its caching means DeepSeek must be using less water and electricity. This cache magic is also how Opus 5.5 quietly got its own efficiency boost.

Yes, I have frontier subscriptions. My work provides Claude, Cursor, and others. I'm not nickel-and-diming here. I'm thinking more about long-term planning, sustainability, and democratizing access to high intelligence. This is a game changer.

These wins are lost on the tech industry, which thinks that if you're not paying top dollar, it's not worth it. FAANG wants to spend the most money for the highest intelligence. Forget it if it's unethical, expensive, or bad for the environment or the economy. This is dog-eat-dog capitalism. This leads to people having crazy setups to load balance a dozen Claude Max subs , and complaining when they can't get more .

And to the self-hosters out there, the economics of 4.1 Flash mean self-hosting is not worth it. If saving money is your goal, you will never recoup the costs. But if your concern is privacy, just wait. These cache optimizations are coming to you, and this cache magic will soon run entirely locally. Even now, 4.1 Flash is technically self-hostable, even if not practically so. Any day now.

items.title: She made India fall in love with women's cricket - now her era as captain is over
items.summary: The skipper who led India to the historic 2025 World Cup win has stepped down from her role in all three formats.
items.content:
When Harmanpreet Kaur scored that unforgettable World Cup century against Australia in the 2017 semi-final, she not only changed the course of a match but the trajectory of women's cricket in India.

India went on to lose the final to England that year but women's cricket no longer remained a passing pursuit for the average Indian fan.

That dogged zeal to win she infused into the team helped them lift India's first women's World Cup trophy - the same feat that had eluded them in 2017 - in emphatic fashion eight years later.

Less than a year on, and within weeks of victories in the Asia Cup and the Asian Games, she has relinquished the captaincy, ending an era in which she became the team's most influential leader and one of the most recognisable figures in the sport.

Star opener Smriti Mandhana, her long-time deputy, has been appointed captain across all formats.

Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) secretary Devajit Saikia, coach Amol Muzumdar, Harmanpreet and Mandhana attended the review meeting at which the leadership change was ratified. The transition, however, was not entirely seamless.

Reports suggest the 37-year-old Harmanpreet was willing to relinquish the T20 captaincy immediately, but was keen to continue leading the side in One-Day Internationals and Tests so that younger players could benefit from her experience.

The BCCI, however, was intent on a younger person at the helm and opted for the 30-year-old Mandhana.

In some ways, the move mirrors the BCCI's decision to replace Suryakumar Yadav as captain of the men's T20 side shortly after India won the World Cup earlier this year, with the captaincy passing to Shreyas Iyer.

Harmanpreet's future as captain had become a subject of intense debate in cricketing circles after India's below-par performance at the T20 World Cup in England a few months ago.

Her own poor form with the bat amplified concerns and prompted the BCCI to consider changes that could help the team meet the growing challenges of a women's game that continues to expand rapidly around the world.

Approaching her 38th birthday, and after almost a decade at the helm, Harmanpreet found herself under increasing scrutiny as her form dipped.

Opinion on whether she should continue as captain was sharply divided among former women players and captains.

Former cricketer Diana Edulji, among the most respected names in the game, felt Harmanpreet had done everything that could reasonably have been expected of her and that it was time for a younger captain to take over. Former captain Anjum Chopra, meanwhile, argued that Harmanpreet's experience remained invaluable and that she should stay on.

Sensing that the BCCI was strongly inclined towards a change, Harmanpreet opted to step down during the review meeting. She later announced her decision in an emotional Instagram post.

"I feel I have done my duty. I gave this team everything I had," she wrote.

"Now, it is time for me to turn the page… Blood. Sweat. Sacrifice. Pride. I gave it all. Now, I'm ready to play for the love of the game again.

Harmanpreet's intention to continue playing now leaves the BCCI with another decision to make about her future.

In Suryakumar Yadav's case, he not only lost the captaincy but also his place in India's T20 side. Given the depth of talent available in the men's game, it was easier for Ajit Agarkar and his fellow selectors to take what was always likely to be a contentious decision.

The situation in the women's game is different. Despite Harmanpreet's modest recent form, replacing a player of her experience and stature may not be straightforward, as the talent pipeline is not yet as deep as it is in men's cricket.

Whatever the future holds, Harmanpreet has scripted among the more memorable careers in women's cricket. Spanning more than two decades, it is a journey marked by significant achievements and milestones.

Born into a family of modest means in Punjab's Moga city, Harmanpreet developed a passion for cricket at an early age.

Her family's support was vital in the early years, but her rise to national recognition came after she joined the Railways - a transition facilitated by Diana Edulji - and moved to Mumbai.

The superior facilities and greater professionalism associated with Mumbai's sporting culture helped accelerate her development.

She made her India debut in 2009 at the age of 20 and has remained an integral part of the national side across formats ever since.

An all-rounder for the better part of her first decade in cricket, she made herself indispensable to the side with her explosive middle-order batting, crafty off-spin and sharp fielding skills.

Her blistering century against Australia in the semi-final of the 2017 Women's ODI World Cup remains one of the defining knocks in the history of the women's game. India went on to lose to England in the final, but beating Australia was a monumental hurdle overcome.

That century also helped spark wider interest in women's cricket in India, and transformed Harmanpreet into a household name.

The second decade of her career showcased her prowess both as batter and captain. Having succeeded Mithali Raj as T20 captain in 2016, Harmanpreet assumed charge across all formats in 2022 and went on to guide India to some of the greatest successes in its history.

Her leadership was marked by an aggressive pursuit of victory. That fearless approach instilled confidence and ambition in her teammates, helping the team overcome even the previously unbeatable Australians, most memorably in the semi-final of the 2025 ODI World Cup.

Unlike in 2017, Harmanpreet couldn't get a hundred on that occasion, but her innings of 89 was a stellar effort as captain. Combined with Jemimah Rodrigues's century, it helped India secure a famous victory over their arch rivals.

India then defeated South Africa in the final to reach what many regard as the pinnacle of achievement in the history of Indian women's cricket.

With multiple titles and trophies won under her leadership, Harmanpreet leaves behind a formidable legacy for her successor, Smriti Mandhana, to emulate.

items.title: Why Zimbabwe tycoon 'Sir Wicknell' was loved and hated in Africa
items.summary: Wicknell Chivayo divided opinion in life and continues to do so in death.
items.content:
Wicknell Chivayo, the Zimbabwean tycoon who died in a helicopter crash along with his wife Lucy Muteke last week, divided opinion in life and continues to do so in death.

He called himself "Sir Wicknell", a nod to the embellishment that epitomised his lifestyle - and a nickname some used for the 45-year-old who packed enough controversy into his short life to last several lifetimes.

He was relentlessly self-documenting, building much of his public persona on social media, where he posed with piles of cash and announced the cars and money he gave to people whom he considered deserving.

Chivayo delighted in displaying his access to heads of state across Africa and showing off his possessions, conducting video tours of his fleet of expensive cars, mainly Rolls-Royces, with vanity plates, watches and a vast collection of designer shoes.

His admirers saw a fabulously wealthy man sharing his good fortune. His detractors recoiled at the ostentatious displays, questioned the origins of his money and his political connections, and saw his lifestyle as a stark illustration of inequality.

But Chivayo remained tone-deaf to such criticism. As his fortunes rose, he became ever more unapologetic about flaunting his wealth in a country where nearly half the population lives below the international poverty line, according to the World Bank.

"He gave to those few on an island of wealth in a sea of poverty," Pedzisai Ruhanya, director of the Zimbabwe Democracy Institute think-tank, told the BBC, explaining how his donations were mainly to influential people.

He dismissed Chivayo's generosity as grandstanding for the ruling Zanu-PF party - an attempt to ensure the support of key politicians and even church leaders.

Nonetheless, there has been an outpouring of grief, especially from recipients of his largesse, and tributes from politicians, religious leaders and business figures.

Among the mourners gathered at the Chivayos' opulent home in the capital, Harare, ahead of their burial on Thursday, was Cleopas Mukungunugwa, a young and prominent Zanu-PF social media influencer and recipient of two luxury cars from Sir Wicknell.

Standing outside the mansion, where a massive poster of the couple is displayed, he told local media that he was devastated by his patron's death , external , explaining how "Sir Wicknell" often dictated what he should write in his posts.

"He was criticised by many on social media and our goal was to bolster his reputation as a philanthropist," he said.

Chivayo dropped out of high school aged 15 because his family could no longer afford the fees after his father died when he was 10.

His first job was as a wages clerk for a bus company. From there, he moved into his first independent hustle - selling mobile phones and dealing in foreign currency, often on the black market at the height of the country's hyperinflation crisis.

In 2005, he was sentenced to five years in prison for money laundering involving 837,000 South African rand (then worth $137,500, £72,000). He served three years at Chikurubi Maximum Prison after two years were suspended.

Details of his career following his release are murky, but he went into the energy business, becoming what one state-run newspaper described as a "tenderpreneur" -making money by getting government contracts.

He headed the firm Intratrek Zimbabwe, which partnered with Chinese electrical giant CHiNT Electric. This was at a time when legislation required all companies in the country to cede economic control to black Zimbabweans, under a policy known as indigenisation.

In 2014, Intratrek was selected to build a 100MW solar power station in the southern town of Gwanda. A contract worth more than $170m was signed the following year. It became one of the biggest controversies of Chivayo's business career.

Zimbabwe Power Company, the state-owned utility that awarded the contract, sought to terminate it when Intratrek failed to deliver, but the courts ultimately ruled that the agreement remained valid.

A parliamentary inquiry later described Intratrek as a "briefcase company" being used as a front to attract investment.

Chivayo acknowledged that Intratrek lacked expertise in solar construction, describing it as the local partner while CHiNT provided the technical muscle.

Intratrek received an advance of more than $5m for the Gwanda solar plant, but it remains unbuilt to this day.

Just weeks before Chivayo's death, Intratrek received a government notice to proceed with the project and was given 24 months to complete it.

As the accusations flew, the businessman just smiled and sweet-talked his way through the maelstrom - even winning over President Emmerson Mnangagwa, who was initially unimpressed by him when he first came to power.

In 2018, Mnangagwa cited Gwanda as a lesson in the dangers of doing business with "fly-by-night briefcase businessmen", adding ominously that "Chikurubi is not full". The state-run Herald newspaper reported that the warning was directed at Chivayo.

Yet within a few years, that relationship transformed into a bromance. In one of several photographs capturing the remarkable informality between them, Chivayo lounges, almost lying, on a sofa beside Mnangagwa, apparently entirely at ease in the president's company.

His access was not confined to Zanu-PF - he also posted photographs with opposition figures, including the late Morgan Tsvangirai and Nelson Chamisa.

But he became a conspicuous presence around Mnangagwa, speaking glowingly of the president and making no secret of his support for Zanu-PF.

He faced allegations over the procurement of materials for the 2023 elections, in which Mnangagwa was voted in for a second term.

Investigations alleged that South African supplier Ren-Form grossly inflated prices and subsequently paid hundreds of millions of rand to a company linked to him. Chivayo denied wrongdoing, and Zimbabwe's anti-corruption commission later said it had found no evidence linking him to procurement fraud. Ren-Form denied any wrongdoing.

In April, he offered the country's 360 legislators $10,000 each, prompting accusations that he wanted to influence an impending vote on a controversial constitutional amendment to extend what would have been Mnangagwa's final five-year term by two years to 2030.

He was forced to withdraw the offer following a backlash and denied it was intended to influence the vote.

When the legislation was signed into law several months later, Zanu-PF posted a video clip of him with the caption , external : "Billionaire Sir Wicknell Chivayo celebrates… singing '2030 Ndeya Emmerson Baba!' while cruising at 51,000 feet aboard his Gulfstream G550".

Access to power became part of Chivayo's social-media persona. In June, Eswatini's King Mswati III granted him citizenship of the southern African kingdom and a diplomatic passport - photographs and videos showed him kneeling before the monarch , external .

He had an impressive camera roll, with snaps of him posing with other African presidents such as Nigeria's Bola Tinubu , external , Tanzania's Samia Suluhu Hassan , external , Malawi's Peter Mutharika , external , Mozambique's Daniel Chapo , external , Zambia's Hakainde Hichilema , external and he was part of the delegation that met South Africa's Cyril Ramaphosa , external when he visited Mnangagwa's farm earlier this year.

Some relationships extended beyond formal meetings. In August, Chivayo and his wife attended the engagement of Kenyan President William Ruto's daughter Charlene at the president's family home.

Afterwards, Ruto personally drove the couple to their waiting helicopter. Chivayo filmed the journey from the passenger seat , external . True to form, he gloated: "Being driven by the president of the republic. God is the greatest."

Ruto wrote on X following the death , external : "I will remember him for his friendship, his energy, and his deep conviction in the possibilities of our continent."

But in Kenya the Zimbabwean businessman was viewed with great suspicion because of his closeness to Ruto - something expressed loudly on social media since his death.

Many of the comments are not printable but as Kenyan blogger Cyprian Nyakundi put it , external , listing some of the controversies surrounding Chivayo: "As a Kenyan, I distance myself completely from President Ruto's glowing tribute to Wicknell Chivayo. Those condolences and that 'dear friend' language are his own, not mine, as a Kenyan."

One commentator on X said his death had "united Africans in celebration" , external .

"When a man's passing brings more relief than sorrow, the reaction itself tells a powerful story. It is time for those in power to reflect and reevaluate!"

At home there has also been pushback against those who say speaking ill of the dead is un-African - as the topic of the tycoon's death is the trending topic in Zimbabwe these days.

At a shopping centre in Harare over the weekend, Christabel Moyo voiced what many have been saying.

"What is African - getting rich from inflated state contracts and using that money to support Zanu-PF?" the 42-year-old accountant asked.

items.title: New York court hears arguments in ongoing 9/11 families' lawsuit against Saudi Arabia
items.summary: The families allege that men with links to the Saudi government helped those who carried out the 2001 attacks, something the country denies.
items.content:
The Court of Appeals in New York has heard arguments from both lawyers for families of 9/11 victims and the government of Saudi Arabia as it decides whether the families' long-running legal case against the Middle Eastern country can move to trial.

Almost 3,000 people were killed on 11 September 2001 after hijackers seized four US passenger jets and crashed them into the World Trade Center in New York, the Pentagon, and a Pennsylvania field, following resistance from passengers.

The families allege that a Saudi government employee, Omar al-Bayoumi, knowingly supported two of the hijackers and that he was working with a network of officials linked to the Saudi Ministry of Islamic Affairs.

Bayoumi, who is now retired from government work, has denied knowing the two men were hijackers or that he had any involvement in 9/11, while Saudi Arabia has said that any allegation that it or its officials are complicit in 9/11 is categorically false.

The Kingdom has argued that, as a foreign sovereign state, it has immunity from prosecution in US courts.

The families, who first filed the lawsuit in 2002, spent several years lobbying US Congress to pass an amendment to the foreign sovereign immunity law to allow the case to go ahead.

In 2016, Congress passed the Justice Against Sponsors of Terrorism Act (JASTA), which allows civil claims against a foreign state or official for injuries, death, or damages from an act of international terrorism.

In August 2025, the Manhattan District Court ruled that the 9/11 families had presented enough evidence to meet the terms of the act and the case was allowed to proceed towards a trial.

Saudi Arabia on Wednesday asked the Court of Appeals to reverse that decision.

Counsel Gregory Rapawy argued core issues of fact – including the central question of the nature of Bayoumi's employment by the Saudi state – had not been decided and needed to be done so before the country could be stripped of immunity.

9/11 families' lawyer Gavin Simpson argued that the District Court had already found that Bayoumi's actions "were not just acts of a good Samaritan or an innocent participant".

"He was, in fact, following Saudi Arabia's instructions when assisting the hijackers," said Simpson, and that these were points that Saudi Arabia had "failed to rebut."

One option the judges seemed to wrestle with was whether to send the case back to the district court to make more concrete findings, which could involve taking testimony from live witnesses.

Asked by Judge Guido Calabresi which witnesses Saudi Arabia could call in that eventuality, Rapawy suggested that if the issue ultimately came down to Bayoumi's credibility, the question of whether he could testify would have to be decided back in the district court.

As he drew the hearing to a close, Judge William Nardini said "it's a difficult case, and we will take it under advisement", meaning that the panel would issue a ruling at a future date.

Speaking outside the courthouse, Terry Strada, whose husband Tom was killed in the World Trade Center, told the BBC she felt positive about the hearing.

"25 years is an extraordinary time to go without accountability and justice for the murder of your loved one. What we hope is that the judges will uphold [District Court] Judge Daniels' decision and move to a trial."

items.title: Guerra Ucraina - Russia, le news dell’8 ottobre. Invito Usa a Parigi, Londra, Berlino, Ue e Nato domani ai colloqui con Kiev
items.summary: Peskov: “D’accordo con Rubio su situazione di stallo”. Zelensky: “Nostri negoziatori in Usa domani e sabato”. Rubio: “Preoccupati che il conflitto in Ucraina si estenda ad altri Paesi”. Raid russo su due autobus a Kramatorsk, 33 morti e 18 feriti. Peskov: “Trump non ha fatto gli auguri a Putin, al momento nessuna data per colloquio tra i due”
items.content:
Non si fermano i raid di Mosca sull’Ucraina. Dopo il brutale attacco alla vigilia del compleanno dello zar che ha colpito un edificio residenziale di cinque piani a Pryluky, nella regione di Chernihiv, uccidendo 19 persone, questa mattina l’esercito russo ha colpito un autobus a Kramatorsk, nel Donetsk, uccidendo 33 persone e ferendone 18.

Intanto, il Cremlino fa sapere che non c'è ancora una data precisa per una telefonata tra il presidente russo Vladimir Putin e il presidente degli Stati Uniti Donald Trump . Mentre il segretario di Stato Usa Marco Rubio parla di una “situazione di stallo strategico in Ucraina” ed esprime la preoccupazione che “il conflitto si estenda ad altri Paesi”.

[[(FckEditorEmbeddedHtmlLayoutElement) Article Embed - rHKMApVNfESObix]]

Peskov: “D’accordo con Rubio sulla fase di stallo nel conflitto”

Negoziatori Kiev domani a Miami, invitati Gb, Francia, Germania, Nato e Ue

Zelensky: “Domani e sabato vedremo negli Usa la delegazione americana”

Telegraph: “Putin affida al ‘generale Armageddon' l'ordine di colpire Kiev”

Zakharova: “Interferenze russe in elezioni in Italia? Irrispettoso”

Seul richiama l'ambasciatore in Ucraina per il caso dei prigionieri nordcoreani

Rubio: “Preoccupati che il conflitto in Ucraina si estenda ad altri Paesi”

Peskov: “D’accordo con Rubio sulla fase di stallo nel conflitto”

Il portavoce del Cremlino Dmitry Peskov ha detto che la Russia concorda con il Segretario di Stato americano Marco Rubio sul fatto che il conflitto in Ucraina si trovi in una fase di stallo. “Sì, siamo d'accordo con lui”, hanno riportato le agenzie di stampa russe citando le parole di Peskov a margine di un incontro dei leader degli Stati dell'ex Unione Sovietica in Turkmenistan. Spetta ai diplomatici, secondo quanto riportato da Peskov, trovare il modo di progredire verso la pace.

Negoziatori Kiev domani a Miami, invitati Gb, Francia, Germania, Nato e Ue

I negoziatori ucraini incontreranno Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner a Miami domani per discutere di "nuove idee e proposte" che gli Stati Uniti hanno iniziato a mettere a punto "con i russi e gli ucraini durante la loro visita". Lo riporta Axios citando alcune fonti, secondo le quali gli Stati Uniti hanno invitato anche i consiglieri alla sicurezza nazionale di Regno Unito, Francia, Germania, ma anche funzionari della Nato e dell'Ue.

Il presidente della Federazione russa Vladimir Putin ha ricevuto nella sua residenza, nel giorno del suo compleanno, l'ex cancelliere tedesco Gerhard Schröder. E' quanto ha riferito il Cremlino. "Ieri mattina, Vladimir Putin ha appreso dai media che Gerhard Schröder si trovava a Mosca per motivi di lavoro. Il presidente ha invitato il suo vecchio amico a raggiungerlo", ha spiegato il Cremlino su Telegram. Proprio ieri Putin festeggiava 74 anni. Il Cremlino ha pubblicato alcune fotografie che mostrano i due uomini mentre si stringono la mano sorridendo. La stampa russa aveva rivelato la scorsa settimana che Schröder, 82 anni, che intrattiene da lungo tempo rapporti con Putin, era stato nominato nel consiglio di sorveglianza di Hyperglobus, una catena di supermercati russa che in passato apparteneva al gruppo tedesco Globus. I legami di Gerhard Schröder, cancelliere tedesco dal 1998 al 2005, con Putin suscitano disagio in Germania, uno dei principali sostenitori dell'Ucraina e Paese che intrattiene rapporti particolarmente tesi con Mosca. Dopo aver lasciato la cancelleria, Schröder aveva già lavorato per il colosso russo del gas Gazprom. Per questo motivo gli erano stati revocati alcuni dei privilegi e dei benefici accordati agli ex capi di governo tedeschi, a causa della sua vicinanza al presidente russo, al quale è rimasto fedele nonostante l'offensiva in Ucraina. Lo scorso maggio, Putin aveva suggerito che l'Europa scegliesse Gerhard Schröder come mediatore per contribuire a risolvere il conflitto. L'ipotesi era stata rapidamente respinta dai 27 Paesi dell'Ue.

L'Alto Commissario delle Nazioni Unite per i diritti umani, Volker Türk, si è detto sconvolto dal "terrificante attacco" compiuto oggi contro due autobus in Ucraina, che ha provocato 30 morti. "La portata e la natura di questi attacchi - che hanno causato la morte e il ferimento di persone a bordo di autobus, nelle loro abitazioni e sui luoghi di lavoro, in diverse regioni del Paese - sono deplorevoli", ha dichiarato in un comunicato.

La squadra di negoziatori ucraini e gli invati del presiente americano, Donald Trump, si vedranno domani e sabato negli Stati Uniti. Lo ha confermato il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky.

L'Ucraina sta preparando una risposta a una nuova ondata di escalation russa e sta collaborando con i partner per ottenere ulteriori pacchetti di difesa aerea e munizioni per i caccia F-16. Lo ha dichiarato il presidente ucraino Volodymyr Zelensky in un messaggio su Telegram. "Un rapporto del capo del Servizio di sicurezza dell'Ucraina, Oleksandr Poklad, e del vice capo dell'Ufficio del Presidente, Pavlo Palisa. Innanzitutto, stiamo preparando le nostre risposte a questa ondata di escalation russa", ha affermato. Ha inoltre sottolineato che l'Ucraina sta lavorando attraverso tutti i canali disponibili con i partner in grado di fornire ulteriore sostegno, inclusi sistemi di difesa aerea e munizioni per gli F-16. Zelensky ha ringraziato tutti i Paesi disposti a offrire aiuto. "In terzo luogo, continuiamo a soddisfare le richieste avanzate dai comandanti dei corpi d'armata e delle brigate durante gli incontri al fronte", ha concluso.

I russi hanno colpito un'importante infrastruttura energetica di Kiev. In alcune zone della capitale si sono verificati blackout. Lo riporta RBC-Ucraina, citando una dichiarazione del ministro dell'Energia Denys Shmyhal e di Ukrenergo. "C'è stato un attacco a uno degli impianti energetici importanti per la città di Kiev. I tecnici del settore energetico stanno facendo tutto il possibile per ripristinare rapidamente l'energia elettrica. Ora continua l'attacco dei droni russi. Sono coinvolti tutti i servizi", ha dichiarato il ministro. Ukrenergo ha dichiarato che, a seguito dell'attacco russo, diversi elementi della rete elettrica che fornisce energia a Kiev sono stati disattivati. Per questo motivo, un numero significativo di consumatori in alcune zone della capitale ha iniziato a subire interruzioni di corrente. "Attualmente, i tecnici del settore energetico stanno ripristinando l'energia elettrica agli utenti a cui è stata interrotta la fornitura. Ci vorrà del tempo. Se ora avete la corrente, vi preghiamo di usarla con parsimonia", ha esortato Ukrenergo. Kyivvodokanal ha riferito che è stata anche registrata una diminuzione della pressione nella rete idrica della parte di Kiev situata sulla riva destra del fiume. "Attualmente si registra un calo di pressione nelle reti idriche della parte della riva destra della capitale, in particolare nei quartieri di Svyatoshynskyi, Solomyanskyi, Shevchenkivskyi, Holosiivskyi e Pechersk. In alcune abitazioni è possibile un'interruzione temporanea dell'erogazione dell'acqua", si legge nel comunicato.

Droni hanno attaccato la raffineria di petrolio di Omsk, in Russia, situata a circa 2.500 chilometri dal confine con l'Ucraina. Secondo quanto riportato da 'Ukrinform', il 'Moscow Times' avrebbe confermato questa notizia. Il governatore della regione di Omsk, Vitaly Khotsenko, ha dichiarato che la regione è stata attaccata da droni ucraini oggi. In precedenza, le autorità locali avevano segnalato restrizioni all'accesso a internet tramite dispositivi mobili e la chiusura dell'aeroporto di Omsk. Nel frattempo, i residenti di Omsk hanno segnalato una serie di esplosioni nei pressi della raffineria di petrolio. "Usciva del fumo dai tubi. Abbiamo sentito due esplosioni", ha raccontato un testimone oculare. La raffineria di petrolio di Omsk, situata a circa 2.500 chilometri dal confine ucraino, è la più grande della Russia. E' di proprietà di Gazprom Neft e può raffinare fino a 22 milioni di tonnellate di petrolio all'anno. Secondo quanto riportato sul sito web della raffineria, l'impianto produce "un sesto di tutti i litri di benzina e gasolio di quinta classe consumati in Russia". I droni ucraini colpirono per la prima volta la raffineria il 6 luglio scorso. L'attacco ha danneggiato le unità di lavorazione primaria del petrolio greggio, costringendo l'impianto a sospendere le operazioni.

"Il meccanismo PURL funziona. E' il più veloce, credo. E' stato avviato a luglio dello scorso anno e ora funziona molto bene, in termini di velocità. L'Ucraina ottiene ciò di cui ha bisogno, in base alle sue richieste e alle sue priorità, e nel modo più rapido. Ma il PURL non è l'unico sistema. L'alleanza ha deciso di fornire all'Ucraina 70 miliardi di dollari quest'anno, il 2026, e la stessa cifra nel 2027. Il solo PURL ha già fornito all'Ucraina sistemi e armamenti per un valore di circa 10 miliardi di dollari. Si tratta di somme enormi e siamo pronti ad intensificare i nostri sforzi per sostenere l'Ucraina in modo sempre più efficace". Lo afferma l'Ammiraglio Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, Presidente del Comitato militare della Nato, intervistato da Ukrinform a Kiev.

items.title: Archaeologists Are Reconstructing the 'Invisible' Technologies of the Stone Age
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.smithsonianmag.com/science-nature/archaeologists-are-reconstructing-the-invisible-technologies-of-the-stone-age-from-rope-to-thread-and-twine-180989534/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49998992 Points: 93 # Comments: 45
items.content:
When an abstract-looking ivory artifact emerged from the Hohle Fels cave in southern Germany in 2015, archaeologists didn’t know quite what to make of it. Previously, this same cave had yielded what may be the world’s oldest musical flutes, as well as one of humanity’s earliest pieces of figurative art, the iconic Venus of Hohle Fels . At first glance, the strange new discovery—a nearly eight-inch rod perforated with four small holes—seemed comparatively unspectacular. But it has since revealed far more about the lives of Europe’s prehistoric hunter-gatherers than its unassuming appearance might have suggested.

Fashioned from the tusk of a mammoth more than 35,000 years ago, this baton—a type of artifact called a lochstab —was initially interpreted as a symbolic object associated with prestige or power. But Nicholas Conard , whose team discovered the item, wasn’t so sure.

Noticing that each of the baton’s holes was lined with carefully carved spiral grooves, he began to suspect that the lochstab might have been a tool used by twisting some other material through the perforations. “If you’re pushing something through a hole and rotating it ... you’re very quickly in the world of fiber,” says Conard, an archaeologist at the University of Tübingen in Germany. Sure enough, when he and his colleagues tried threading cattail fibers through these holes, they found that the grooves helped to orient the strands . Within ten minutes, the group had woven the fibers into 16 feet of thick, strong rope.

Yet while these experiments might have helped to solve one archaeological mystery, they also highlighted a much larger problem. The inhabitants of Hohle Fels must have manufactured significant quantities of rope, but none of it has survived. All that remains is the most durable component of this ancient production system—the ivory lochstab.

“There’s certainly a lot of bias in what we’re viewing in the archaeological record, because we are focusing on the things that preserve,” says paleoanthropologist Emma Finestone at the Cleveland Museum of Natural History. As a consequence, archaeologists rely heavily on stone tools and bone artifacts to reconstruct our prehistory, while objects made from less durable plant and animal products remain largely overlooked. Yet these soft technologies played a huge role in shaping the survival strategies and daily lives of our ancestors.

“We’re missing 90 percent-plus of what is happening during a [prehistoric] day, and a lot of that uses technology that we don’t think about,” says Bruce Hardy , a paleoanthropologist at Kenyon College in Ohio. The problem facing archaeologists, therefore, is how to study a technology that is, in a sense, invisible—a technology they can’t actually find.

The oldest surviving example of human-made fiber is a six-millimeter-long piece of string made by Neanderthals some 50,000 years ago. It’s an exceedingly rare example of preserved ancient fiber , and how it managed to withstand the ravages of time isn’t clear. Discovered by Hardy and his colleagues at the Abri du Maras rock shelter in France, this small length of three-ply cord indicates that fiber has deep roots in the human lineage.

“This is probably a very old technology that goes way back much further than this, back to an ancestor shared by modern humans and Neanderthals,” Hardy says. In other words, more than half a million years ago .

So far, the oldest evidence of fiber use dates back about 250,000 years, inferred from markings on stone tools from France and the Netherlands. The marks suggest the tools may have been hafted, or attached to a handle with some type of string or cord. While the bindings have long since decomposed, the traces they left behind hint that fiber technologies aided the survival of the prehistoric human species that occupied Europe long before Homo sapiens got a foothold on the continent 45,000 years ago.

The invention of hafting may represent a “revolutionary moment” in our technological history, says Veerle Rots , an archaeologist at the University of Liège in Belgium who led the experimental work on the Hohle Fels lochstab. “It fundamentally changes the use of stone tools and allows a whole range of new possibilities in how you’re conceptualizing a tool,” she says.

A sharpened stone point, for example, suddenly becomes part of a hunting weapon when hafted onto a wooden shaft. A stone handax can be wielded with significantly greater force and from a wider range of angles once fastened onto a handle. What made cordage like rope, string and twine so transformative, therefore, was that it connected other technologies together to radically expand what prehistoric humans could build, carry and hunt.

The transport of stone for making tools, for instance, was an essential logistical operation that may have depended on soft materials from the very beginning. According to Finestone’s research, toolmaking hominins moved high-quality stones over long distances as early as three million years ago —cumbersome loads that would have been very difficult to transport with bare hands alone.

“It would have been really helpful to them to have some mechanism for carrying cobbles,” she says. Such receptacles have never been found. But if they were used, they were probably made from perishable materials like leather and fiber.

Cordage likely also aided our ancestors by enabling passive hunting with snares and nets. Unlike handheld weapons, these tools could catch prey in the user’s absence, allowing hunter-gatherers to focus on other tasks. Rock art in Spain from around 7,500 years ago even appears to depict people climbing sophisticated rope ladders to access beehives, illustrating how fiber technologies opened up new foraging opportunities.

“Once you figure out this technology, you’re just going to keep applying it,” says Hardy. “You’re going to become dependent on it.”

In a cave in Oregon, researchers discovered two pieces of 12,000-year-old elk hide stitched together with a cord -the oldest known remains of sewn animal hide . (Indirect evidence of sewing, such as needles with eyes for threading string, has been found from longer ago throughout the world.)

As cordage became essential for survival, the need to continually produce it fundamentally shaped the daily routines of ancient hunter-gatherers, Hardy says.

“You find out very rapidly that you need a lot of footage of cord in order to make anything,” he says. One year in a class he taught, Hardy and his students built a raft out of sycamore saplings lashed together with what he estimates was just over 100 yards of rope. “It was hours and hours and hours of making cordage to do that.”

Ethnographic studies of present-day traditional societies attest to the labor involved. The Wola of Papua New Guinea, for example, incorporate string or fibers into 95 percent of the items they produce, from hunting weapons to musical instruments. Anthropologists have found that it takes the Wola between 65 and 80 hours of twisting to generate enough string to manufacture a single bag—and that’s on top of 14 hours of foraging to collect the raw materials. Given that the Wola live in permanent villages, this time investment may not present any major issues, but for nomadic hunter-gatherers, the need to produce such enormous quantities of cordage would have significantly impacted their ability to move around.

The Neanderthals of Abri du Maras, for example, made their cord from the inner bark of pine or another conifer, which can be harvested only in the spring and early summer, when the sap begins to rise and the inner bark thickens. Once collected, the bark must be soaked in water for about two weeks before it can be broken up into usable fibers.

The lengthy nature of this process would therefore have dictated the seasonal work schedule of mobile hunter-gatherers, who would not be able to move on until a sufficient quantity of cordage had been manufactured. “It’s going to be impacting your daily life,” says Hardy. “You’re going to be making cordage all the time, at least during certain times of year, and storing it up.”

So, while stone flakes for use as cutting tools, scrapers and weapons could be struck from larger chunks of flint whenever needed, activities like rope making, hide tanning and woodworking required seasonal planning, sustained labor and group decision-making.

The more researchers discover about these soft materials, the more they understand about how these technologies defined the rhythm of everyday life in the Stone Age , the large swath of human history from about 3.3 million to 4,000 years ago. “We’ll learn some new stuff from stone tools and from animal bones, but we’re not going to see this other side of daily life that is going on unless we can see the perishable material,” says Hardy.

That material isn’t just limited to fiber. At an ancient lakeshore exposed by a mine near Schöningen, Germany, archaeologists discovered a remarkable assemblage of 300,000-year-old wooden spears , along with bones of some of the horses and other animals they were used to kill. The spears survived because anaerobic conditions at the waterlogged site prevented microorganisms from breaking them down. Made by an extinct human species, these remarkable weapons were expertly worked into aerodynamic forms, thus enhancing their lethality and revealing a level of technological sophistication that stone tools alone fail to capture.

items.title: Il futuro di Windows 11 è un PC con Copilot che usa il computer al posto tuo
items.summary: Windows traccia la strada per un futuro dove desktop e AI si dovranno inevitabilmente incontrare: nelle prossime versioni del sistema operativo arriverà la ricerca nella taskbar con azioni rapide, Copilot organizzerà e modificherà i file del PC e le app Windows saranno create da un prompt. Usando IA locale e in cloud. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Se fino a oggi chi ha usato Windows è stato abituato ad usare una tastiera, un mouse e un trackpad per spostare file, aprire applicazioni e muoversi in un ambiente che è rimasto praticamente identico per oltre vent’anni, tra qualche mese ci sarà una possibilità in più.

Si potrà infatti dire cosa si vuole ottenere e lasciare che Windows, "con il permesso dell’utente", porti a termine la cosa da solo.

Microsoft, durante la conferenza di lancio del nuovo Surface Laptop Ultra, ha tracciato questa mattina la strada che dovrebbe finalmente portare Windows e l’IA a incontrarsi senza gli intoppi del recente passato, dove l’IA è stata inserita un po’ ovunque senza un briciolo di criterio. Con l’unico risultato, molti se lo ricorderanno, di dover fare un dietrofront dopo le numerose proteste degli utenti.

Microsoft non può tenere fuori l’IA da Windows , è evidente, ma non può nemmeno cambiare il modo in cui le persone hanno usato il computer fino a ora senza poter dare diverse opzioni.

La nuova strategia sembra quindi decisamente più interessante di quella che abbiamo visto quando l’IA in Windows serviva solo a trasformare uno schizzo in un disegno all’interno di Paint, e invece di mettere l’IA dentro ogni singola app Microsoft ha pensato di cucirla all’interno del sistema operativo stesso, lavorando su tre elementi. La ricerca nella taskbar, finalmente migliorata e potenziata dall’IA, Copilot, che finalmente conosce i file e le impostazioni del computer e può usarli e modificarli e un’intelligenza artificiale "ibrida" che sceglie se lavorare in locale o nel cloud, perché l’IA locale non è al momento efficiente e precisa quanto un modello cloud nei compiti più complessi.

Per Microsoft la ricerca nella taskbar è il punto da cui centinaia di milioni di persone ogni giorno partono se hanno bisogno di qualcosa, che sia un file o un’app, e da questo autunno su Windows 11 non servirà più solo a trovare app, impostazioni e file, ma anche a eseguire migliaia di azioni rapide.

Si potrà passare alla modalità scura, attivare "non disturbare", alzare il volume del microfono con uno slider direttamente dentro i risultati, fare uno screenshot o disporre le finestre.

Si potrà anche inviare un SMS a un amico o a un collega, per avvisare di un ritardo, senza tirare fuori il telefono dalla tasca, sempre che lo smartphone sia collegato.

Se la richiesta è complessa, la ricerca passa il testimone a Copilot: una domanda veloce riceve risposta direttamente nella casella di ricerca, mentre se si chiede qualcosa di più complesso, che richiede un ragionamento o un tempo di attesa superiore a pochi istanti, la conversazione si sposta nell’app Copilot. Che ora conosce il PC e lo può modificare.

Il cambiamento più radicale riguarda l’app Copilot, che cerca di difendere la sua posizione privilegiata di assistente preinstallato da ChatGPT e Claude, che non vedono l’ora di piazzare il loro client su Windows con tanto di capacità agentiche.

Copilot su Windows ottiene tre capacità nuove, e la prima è il local context, ovvero la possibilità di ragionare su tutti i file presenti sul PC, creando un database di contesto che memorizza esattamente cosa c’è in ogni file, quando è stato creato e perché.

La seconda sono le local actions: Copilot può compiere azioni direttamente sul computer, per esempio spostare file o cambiare un’impostazione, con lo stesso livello di controllo che ha l’utente, ma sempre chiedendo il permesso.

La terza sono i local models: per i compiti più difficili si continua a usare il cloud, ma quando contano di più i costi o la riservatezza Copilot può delegare il lavoro a modelli che girano sul computer, sempre che il computer possa gestire questi modelli, e i nuovi RTX Spark sembrano fatti apposta per quello.

Del nuovo Copilot ne abbiamo già parlato quando Microsoft lo ha presentato le scorse settimane, ed è un’applicazione con diverse modalità, tra le quali troviamo anche Code e Autopilot.

Code porterà il vibe coding dentro Windows e, secondo Microsoft, sarà “semplice per chiunque costruire e condividere un’app, senza esperienza da sviluppatori”. L’azienda è infatti convinta che ognuno potrà costruire un’app Windows nativa partendo da un singolo prompt.

Autopilot sarà invece l’agente autonomo: nella demo che Microsoft ha mostrato di una persona che deve inviare documenti per le tasse, l’agente ha trovato da solo nella posta l’email del commercialista con l’elenco dei documenti necessari, poi ha cercato i file sparsi tra Download e Documenti (metà in ordine, metà no), li ha spostati in una nuova cartella, li ha rinominati, ha creato delle sottocartelle, ha compresso tutto in un unico ZIP e ha preparato l’email di risposta con l’allegato. A quel punto si ferma e chiede conferma prima di inviare.

Microsoft chiarisce che l’organizzazione e la rinomina dei file avvengono con modelli locali, quindi i dati fiscali non finiscono nel cloud.

Inutile raccontarci che si può fare tutto con l’IA locale: non si può, sempre che non si abbia una macchina con 128 GB di RAM e potenza da vendere accesa 24 ore su 24. Il cloud continua e continuerà a essere la scelta predefinita per i compiti più pesanti, ma una parte sempre maggiore del lavoro potrà restare sul computer in locale, per ragioni di riservatezza e di costo.

A decidere cosa resta in locale e cosa va nel cloud è il routing, e qui entra in gioco Hydrafusion, il sistema annunciato quest’anno da GitHub che smista ogni attività verso il modello più adatto. Microsoft ha annunciato oggi che Hydrafusion arriva su Windows e, oltre a scegliere tra il modello più adatto in cloud, p otrà anche pescare tra i modelli che girano in locale sul PC.

Nella demo che Microsoft ha fatto vedere si vede chiaramente come lavori semplici, come la pulizia del codice, vengano affidati automaticamente a un modello locale, mentre un’analisi più complessa parte da una sessione cloud che può però delegare a sottosessioni locali per risparmiare token.

Per dimostrare quanto oggi siano capaci i modelli in locale e quanto possano mantenere le loro capacità nonostante una forte quantizzazione, Microsoft ha fatto alcuni esempi di modelli molto grandi compressi per stare in un PC. MAI Code 1.1 Flash, modello da 130 miliardi di parametri per il codice, è stato portato a tre bit di precisione e, grazie alla quantizzazione, riduce di quasi l’80% le dimensioni, mantenendo però una finestra di contesto da 256K.

DeepSeek V4 Flash, 284 miliardi di parametri a 1,6 bit, entra in circa 60 GB e, secondo Microsoft, supera GPT-5 nei benchmark di coding e reasoning: DeepSeek V4 Flash gira senza problemi su RTX Spark da 128 GB. Altri modelli super efficienti ma piccoli arriveranno nei prossimi mesi.

items.title: Surface Laptop Ultra ufficiale. L’anti MacBook Pro di Microsoft parte da 2.599 dollari
items.summary: 15 pollici, un petaflop di potenza di calcolo AI, SSD removibile e configurazioni fino a 128 GB di memoria. Microsoft posiziona il suo nuovo Surface Laptop Ultra allo stesso prezzo dei MacBook Pro: la sfida è iniziata. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Surface Laptop Ultra, il modello di punta della famiglia Surface che Microsoft ha preparato insieme a NVIDIA per essere il “reference design” da cui trarre ispirazione per progettare le workstation Windows del futuro, ha finalmente un prezzo e una data di uscita. I preordini partono oggi, il laptop verrà consegnato a partire da metà ottobre anche se in Italia potrebbe non arrivare subito, ma qualche mese dopo.

Secondo Pavan Davuluri, il responsabile della divisione hardware e Windows di Microsoft, è " il Surface più potente mai costruito " ed è evidente, dopo il lancio degli altri prodotti Surface con processore Snapdragon avvenuti nei mesi scorsi, che Microsoft per la parte consumer e prosumer sta puntando esclusivamente sull’architettura ARM.

Qualcomm presta i suoi Snapdragon X2 Plus ai Surface Pro e ai Surface Laptop, NVIDIA guarda invece al segmento prosumer con l’Ultra che punta a prendere il posto, nelle prossime generazioni, di quelle che fino a oggi sono state le workstation con CPU x86 accompagnate da GPU esterna RTX.

Il cuore di Surface Ultra è RTX Spark, con il superchip NVIDIA disponibile nelle due varianti con GPU Blackwell RTX da 5.120 core e CPU Grace a 18 core e con GPU da 6.144 core e CPU Grace a 20 core. La memoria è LPDDR5x unificata con tagli da 24, 32, 48, 64 e 128 GB, la stessa architettura alla base dei MacBook Pro con i quali Microsoft vuole andare a competere direttamente. Il target è quello classico di Apple: content creator, sviluppatori, designer, fotografi, ma anche giocatori, visto che, come ha ricordato Jensen Huang dal palco della conferenza Microsoft di San Francisco, RTX Spark è l’unico computer al mondo in grado di eseguire nativamente DirectX, OpenGL e le applicazioni CUDA, con oltre 1.200 applicazioni testate.

Tornando al laptop, siamo davanti a un design totalmente nuovo costruito attorno al processore NVIDIA: il display è un PixelSense Ultra touch da 15 pollici, con luminosità di 1.000 nit in SDR e picchi di 2.000 nit in HDR. Per Microsoft è lo schermo per laptop con la più alta luminosità di picco HDR mai realizzato. La scocca, in alluminio, fa segnare sulla bilancia 2 kg di peso, con uno spessore che resta sotto i 18 mm nella parte più spessa. La dotazione di porte è la più ricca mai vista su un Surface: USB-C/USB4, HDMI 2.1b, USB-A 3.1, lettore SD e jack da 3,5 mm.

Debutta anche Magnetic Connect, la prima porta USB-C magnetica al mondo: siamo davanti a una classica presa USB dotata però di due magneti ai lati che guidano l’inserimento di un connettore simile all’USB, ma non standard. È più corto, sottile e, se si inciampa nel filo, esce senza problemi, al contrario di quello classico USB, che si innesta invece con precisione e deve essere estratto con un movimento assiale. Una connessione semi-proprietaria, perché il laptop si può ricaricare con ogni caricatore, la porta è una vera USB, ma il caricatore del Surface può essere usato solo con questa porta perché la spina è diversa.

Surface Laptop Ultra è touchscreen e ha un qualcosa che i MacBook Pro non hanno, ovvero l’SSD removibile. È il classico connettore M.2, Gen 4 nella versione da 512 GB e Gen 5 da 1 e 2 TB.

Sul fronte dell’autonomia, Microsoft dichiara fino a 15 ore di riproduzione video locale e fino a 12 ore di navigazione web attiva, misurate su un sample di pre-produzione nella configurazione top (GPU da 6.144 core, 64 GB di RAM, 1 TB di storage) con schermo a 150 nit.

Ricorda inoltre che le prestazioni non variano se si usa il laptop a batteria, che è un po’ un unicum per una workstation con NVIDIA RTX, dove solitamente, senza l’alimentatore da 300 Watt, le prestazioni si dimezzavano.

Per Microsoft questa macchina è la vera alternativa al MacBook Pro M5 Pro per chi vuole Windows, e non è un caso che durante la conferenza abbia proprio fatto un confronto con la workstation Apple, dicendo che su alcuni modelli LLM Surface Laptop Ultra offre un time to first token più rapido per i modelli linguistici e tempi di generazione delle immagini più brevi rispetto ai portatili con M5 Pro.

Capitolo prezzi, come sempre da valutare nell’ambito dei prezzi americani, che sono esentasse: si parte da 2.599,99 dollari per la versione di ingresso, che ha RTX Spark con GPU da 5.120 core e CPU a 18 core, 24 GB di memoria unificata, 512 GB di SSD, Windows 11 Home e finitura Platinum. Con la stessa configurazione, ma 1 TB di storage, il prezzo sale a 2.999,99 dollari, e a quel punto si può scegliere anche il colore Nightfall. È lo stesso prezzo del MacBook Pro M5 Pro da 16”.

Restando sulla versione meno potente del SoC, se si sale a 32 GB di memoria, con 1 TB di SSD e Windows 11 Pro, il listino sale a 3.299,99 dollari, con il prezzo che cresce ancora se si vuole la versione più potente di RTX Spark, con GPU da 6.144 core e CPU a 20 core: 3.699,99 dollari.

A fare la differenza a questo punto è solo la “costosa” RAM: con 48 GB si arriva a 3.999,99 dollari, con 64 GB a 4.299,99 dollari e con 128 GB a 5.899,99 dollari.

items.title: Eritrean troops move deep into Ethiopia's Tigray region, residents tell BBC
items.summary: Residents of Adigrat tell the BBC they have seen truck loads of soldiers from Eritrea moving south.
items.content:
Eritrean soldiers have crossed into northern Ethiopia heading towards an area where clashes have been taking place between national army troops and regional forces, residents in the Tigrayan town of Adigrat have told the BBC.

Fighting in the region broke out two weeks ago after months of tension between the government and the party that controls Tigray, the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF). Both blame one another for violating a 2022 deal that ended a two-year civil war.

Ethiopia has also accused Eritrea of backing the TPLF - something Asmara has previously denied.

The latest unrest follows the launch in September of new alliance of armed groups in Ethiopia, which includes the TPLF.

How fresh fighting in Tigray could spark wider conflict in Ethiopia

The young women who fought in Ethiopia's last civil war and don't want to see another one

Over the weekend, TPLF forces withdrew from Tigray's main city of Mekelle, which is 115km (71 miles) south of Adigrat and is now under army control.

Eritrea was a key ally of landlocked Ethiopia during the 2020-2022 war, fighting against the TPLF in what was one of the most deadly conflicts this century and which drove the Tigray region to the precipice of famine.

But relations between the two neighbours have since deteriorated largely over the Ethiopian prime minister's ambition to take ownership of one of Eritrea's Red Sea ports.

Last week the two countries severed diplomatic relations as the renewed fighting raised fears of a wider regional conflict.

The BBC is unable to report from Tigray and surrounding areas, though mobile phone connections and internet access have been restored to most areas since the military took over Mekelle.

According to multiple accounts, Eritrean troops have moved from the border town of Zalambessa towards central Tigray, with convoys reportedly passing through Adigrat and heading toward Edaga Hamus, a town between Adigrat and Mekelle.

"I saw about 40 trucks carrying soldiers. The convoy was moving south," one resident of Adigrat, who requested anonymity for security reasons, told BBC Tigrinya.

A second resident reported seeing troop movements, initially at night: "We have been seeing trucks with Eritrean registration plates passing through the city.

"Now this morning we witnessed around 20 to 30 large trucks heading toward Edaga Hamus."

He added that acquaintances travelling along the route had seen additional vehicles carrying heavy weapons, including anti-aircraft guns, and noted some troops were also moving on foot.

A source in Mekelle told the BBC that relatives in Adigrat described even larger troop movements, and estimated they saw up to 60 trucks carrying soldiers who were later deployed in mountainous terrain near Edaga Hamus.

Images circulating on social media appear to show heavily loaded military trucks carrying uniformed personnel towards Adigrat, Edaga Hamus and possibly Wukro, another key town along the corridor between Adigrat and Mekelle. The BBC has not independently verified the images.

Sources in Wukro told the BBC that national army soldiers and allied fighters had entered the town on Wednesday after an exchange of heavy weapons about 15km south of the town.

The BBC has not yet been able to independently verify any of the reported troop movements.

The reported return of Eritrean forces has sparked anxiety among many of Tigray's residents, with some recalling the atrocities allegedly committed by soldiers from Eritrea during the recent civil war , when they fought against the TPLF.

One Adigrat resident said that seeing Eritrean soldiers again was emotionally distressing: "The memories are still fresh. I was emotional myself. People are saddened to see them back again."

A resident of Edaga Hamus also reported Eritrean troops passing through the town and said drone strikes had occurred nearby, with soldiers targeted.

In a recent interview with private station Fana Television, senior Ethiopian government official Abraham Belay accused Eritrea of direct participation in the conflict.

"The Eritrean army has participated with its full capacity and logistics," he said.

"Many Eritrean soldiers have been killed and captured. There is no doubt that the retaliation will be double. They will see what it means to enter the border of another country and fight alongside bandits."

items.title: A 5.3M-year-old deep-sea whale necropolis in the Diamantina Zone
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-10546-z Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49996639 Points: 69 # Comments: 2
items.content:
Whale falls are biodiversity oases at seabeds 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 , 5 , 6 , yet their record from the oceans has remained sparse and fragmentary 6 , 7 . Here we report the discovery of a vast whale necropolis in the Diamantina Zone (4,616- to 7,001-m depth), extending about 1,200 km along the sea floor of the southeastern Indian Ocean. This area has a deep and extensive accumulation comprising five modern natural whale-fall communities and 476 fossil cetaceans recorded. We show that carcasses host specialized communities dominated by brittle stars, bone-boring worms and chemosynthesis-based bivalves and that the fossil record in this area comprises both extant and extinct deep-diving beaked whales. Isotopic dating shows that whale falls in this region have occurred since at least 5.3 million years ago. These findings reshape the understanding of the limits and biogeography of whale-fall ecosystems and establish some deep sea floors as a fossil archive for tracing cetacean evolution over geological time.

The deep sea is home to myriad life forms that have adapted to extreme environmental conditions. One of the most fascinating phenomena of the deep sea are whale-fall communities, whereby a whale carcass that sinks to the ocean floor 1 , 2 , 3 initiates a highly idiosyncratic ecosystem in association with a variety of physiologically diverse organisms, thus providing crucial insights into the interplay of life and death in the ocean’s depths 4 , 5 , 6 , 7 . Although whale falls are abundant, with more than 70 sites documented across diverse ocean basins and depths 6 , their distribution remains patchy and only sporadically documented 7 .

The species composition and diversity of whale-fall communities are strongly influenced by water depth and related environmental factors, such as temperature and hydrodynamic regime 6 , 8 , 9 . In contrast to deep-sea sites, shallow-water shelf whale falls generally yield different sets of taxa, indicating that highly specialized and species-rich whale-fall communities develop primarily in the food-limited setting of the deep ocean 7 , 10 , 11 , 12 , 13 . So far, however, most whale falls are found between some tens of metres to around 4,000 m water depth 6 , 7 , with the deepest example reaching 4,204 m in the southwest Atlantic Ocean 14 . The biogeography, evolutionary novelty and connectivity of deep-sea whale-fall communities remain poorly understood, first and foremost because of the paucity of data from abyssal and hadal depths 7 .

The Diamantina Fracture Zone lies to the south of the Broken Ridge and Perth Abyssal Plain in the Indian Ocean, stretching about 1,200 km parallel to the Southeast Indian Ridge (Fig. 1 ). It formed as the Australian and Antarctic continents separated between 60 million and 50 million years ago 15 . The rough sea floor topology is the result of block faulting 16 . The deepest regions of the Diamantina Zone cluster in its northwestern section, most notably at the Dordrecht Deep, which reaches a maximum depth of 7,079 m as measured by the conductivity–temperature–depth sensor aboard the human-occupied vehicle (HOV) Fendouzhe in 2023. The Diamantina Zone has not been previously documented to be associated with any whale falls.

From 8 February to 17 March 2023, using the Fendouzhe submersible capable of reaching depths of up to 11,000 m on board the R/V Tansuoyihao , we discovered extensive whale falls and fossils in the Diamantina Zone (Fig. 1 and Supplementary Video 1 ). During dive FDZ159, we first encountered whale fossils at a depth of 7,002 m, near the deepest point of the Dordrecht Deep. These fossils were found partially buried in soft surface sediments and lightly coated with black Fe–Mn oxides. Following the initial discovery, we conducted 32 dives to the sea floor, aiming at mapping the spatial distribution and extent of the whale falls and fossils, as well as identifying any associated whale-fall ecosystems. By doing this, we documented and collected samples from 485 whale-fossil sites and active whale falls (Fig. 2 , Extended Data Tables 1 and 2 and Supplementary Table 1 ) from 1,200 km along the sea floor, representing an ecological landmark in the Diamantina Zone.

The five active whale falls are in the sulfophilic stage (Fig. 2 ). Bones are covered with dense, whitish microbial mats and bone-boring worms Osedax , indicating prolonged residence on the sea floor. At 6,789 m water depth, the Dordrecht Deep beaked-whale carcass WF1, consisting of three elongated vertebrae, has the deepest active whale-fall community. The largest carcass encountered, the 5-m-long skeleton WF3, was identified as the Antarctic minke whale Balaenoptera bonaerensis through the highly diagnostic earbone morphology 17 and a nearly complete mitochondrial genome (GenBank: PX519993 ).

Across the five whale falls in the sulfophilic stage, the associated fauna are taxonomically broad, comprising 35 recognized macrofaunal taxa (more than 0.5 mm in size) documented from in situ imagery and collected specimens (Extended Data Table 1 and Extended Data Figs. 1 and 2 ). The macrofauna are dominated by annelids, crustaceans and molluscs, with further cnidarians and nematodes. Bone-eating worms, gastropods, vesicomyid bivalves and brittle stars dominate the megafauna (more than several centimetres in size), reaching local densities up to 2,840 individuals per square metre (Supplementary Table 2 ).

Most recovered taxa may be new to science. Molecular data were obtained for 21 species, but only the vesicomyid bivalve Abyssogena southwardae could be confidently assigned to species level through barcoding comparison with GenBank records; all remaining species were identified at genus or family rank, integrating morphological data. Three chemosymbiotic bivalves ( Adipicola sp., Abyssogena southwardae and Thyasiridae sp.) hosting different sulfur-oxidizing microbial symbionts (Extended Data Fig. 2 ) and two bone-eating worms ( Osedax sp. 1 and Osedax sp. 2) form the core of these communities 18 , 19 . The observations at water depths of 5,609 m and 5,634 m of sea daisies (Asteroidea: Xyloplax sp.) provide, to our knowledge, the deepest evidence of this genus, as well as the first record on whale falls, expanding the habitat of Xyloplax beyond wood falls and hydrothermal vents 20 . Three brittle-star species ( Ophiambix sp., Ophioscolecidae gen. et sp. and Silax sp.) recovered from the whale skeletons differ notably from the dominant trench-floor ophiuroid genera Ophiosphalma and Ophiuroglypha . The absence of whale-fall species in the background sediments indicates that these brittle-star assemblages are highly specialized and confined to organic-rich whale substrates. In addition, some whale falls, for instance, at depths of 5,115 m, 6,470 m, 6,570 m and 6,772 m, are in the final reef stage (Extended Data Fig. 3 ). The exterior of these skeletons is primarily inhabited by common hard-substrate megafauna, such as the stalked sea anemone Galatheanthemum profundale , the pedunculate sponge Caulophacus sp. and the sea star Freyastera sp. The different faunal composition of the studied whale falls may be attributable to their sites, successional stages or carcass sizes.

The palaeontological analysis of 43 recovered fossils from the Diamantina Zone led to the identification of five beaked-whale species and one baleen-whale species. Most of the beaked-whale specimens, primarily consisting of isolated rostra, were attributed to two living ziphiid species: the Andrews’ beaked whale, Mesoplodon bowdoini (Fig. 3a,b ), and the strap-toothed whale, Mesoplodon layardii (Fig. 3c,d ), both of which are known to inhabit the present-day southeastern Indian Ocean 21 . Diagnostic traits of M. layardii preserved in 14 specimens include a narrow, elongated, transversely compressed rostrum and a strongly pachyosteosclerotic vomer forming a prominent posterior bulge, a secondary anterior bulge and a midrostral dorsal depression in between (Fig. 3c,d and Extended Data Fig. 4a–g ). Further matching traits, such as the shape of the prominential notch and maxillary tubercle and the size and position of the infraorbital and premaxillary foramina, further support this identification 22 . The seven rostra assigned to M. bowdoini are robust, moderately elongated and laterally compressed and provided with a single anterior vomeral bulge and a ventrally deflected apex, consistent with previous descriptions 22 (Fig. 3a,b and Extended Data Fig. 4e–h ).

Three exceptionally well-preserved skulls were identified as belonging to the extinct genera Pterocetus and Izikoziphius , which were first described from fossils trawled from the sea floor off South Africa 23 . As for Pterocetus , this extinct relative of the modern Mesoplodon spp. and bottlenose beaked whales is characterized by distinctive wing-like expansions of the preorbital processes 23 . One Pterocetus specimen from the Diamantina Zone is referred to P. benguelae (Fig. 3h ); the other represents a new species, Pterocetus diamantinae sp. nov. ( Supplementary Note , Fig. 3e–g , Extended Data Figs. 5 a,b and 6 and Extended Data Table 3 ). The single Izikoziphius cranium closely resembles the type species I. rossi (Fig. 3i and Extended Data Fig. 5e,f ). Izikoziphius is a close relative of the extant Cuvier’s beaked whale but is recognized as a separate genus owing to the observation of a unique fossa on the premaxilla, a dome-shaped maxillary crest and a proportionally longer rostrum 23 . Baleen-whale fossils include a fairly well-preserved tympanic bulla of the sei whale, Balaenoptera borealis (Extended Data Fig. 5g–j ) and several dilapidated, largely indeterminate cranial and postcranial remains of mostly balaenopterid mysticetes (Extended Data Fig. 5k–l ).
